title: Find the K-or of an Array
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. Their K-or is a number built one bit position at a time: a position holds a 1 in the K-or exactly when `k` or more of the values in `nums` have a 1 at that position, and holds a 0 otherwise. Return the K-or of `nums`.

With `k = 1` this is just the ordinary bitwise OR of all the values.
notes:
## Intuition

Bit positions do not influence each other here: whether position `b` ends up set depends only on how many values have a 1 at `b`. So the whole task splits into 31 tiny counting problems, one per position (values stay below 2^31, so positions 0 to 30 are enough). For each position, count the values that have that bit, and switch the bit on in the answer when the count reaches `k`.

## Approach

1. Start `result` at 0.
2. For every `bit` from 0 to 30, build `mask = 1 << bit`, a number with only that bit on.
3. Walk through `nums` and increase `count` for each `num` where `num & mask` is non-zero.
4. If `count >= k`, turn the bit on with `result |= mask`.
5. After all positions, return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [7, 12, 9, 8, 9, 15]`, `k = 4`.

- `bit = 0` (`mask = 1`): 7, 9, 9 and 15 are odd, so `count = 4`. That reaches `k`, and `result` becomes 1.
- `bit = 1` (`mask = 2`): only 7 and 15, `count = 2`. Skipped.
- `bit = 2` (`mask = 4`): 7, 12 and 15, `count = 3`. Skipped.
- `bit = 3` (`mask = 8`): 12, 9, 8, 9 and 15, `count = 5`. `result` becomes `1 | 8 = 9`.
- Every higher bit has `count = 0`, so the answer is `9`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(31 · n): each of the 31 positions scans the array once.
- Space: O(1): only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- Test a bit with `(num & mask) !== 0`; parenthesise the `&`, since `!==` binds more tightly than `&` in JavaScript.
- Stop at bit 30. `1 << 31` is negative in JavaScript, and no value can have that bit anyway.
- The threshold is "at least `k`", so compare with `>=`, not `>` or `===`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | the K-or built so far |
| `bit` | the position being examined |
| `mask` | a number with only `bit` set |
| `count` | how many values have `bit` set |
| `num` | the value currently tested |

narration.2: The answer starts with every bit off.
narration.3: Look at each bit position from 0 to 30 on its own, since positions never affect each other.
narration.4: Build a number whose only 1 is at this position.
narration.5: Reset the tally of values that have this bit.
narration.6: Go through every value in nums.
narration.7: AND with the mask keeps just this bit, so a non-zero result means the value has it.
narration.8: One more value has this bit set.
narration.11: Did at least k values have this bit?
narration.12: Yes: switch the same bit on in the answer.
narration.15: All positions are decided; return the K-or.
